decisions.selected: Deliver an ACE session link in a pull-request comment after /ace.
alternatives: Count workflow runs or generated text.
decisions.rationale: The workflow description, action step, and evals explicitly require a session link and posted comment.
The slash command is the explicit user request and identifies the pull request.

decisions.selected: Use archived case/event PR number, then reconstruct from the latest qualifying /ace comment before run creation.
decisions.rationale: The primary binding is deterministic when archived metadata exists; the fallback preserves historical runs with null case and event.

decisions.selected: Same-repository pull-request issue comment containing the exact generated ACE URL by cutoff.
decisions.rationale: The workflow's GitHub Script creates the operational artifact directly; repository comments are observable and auditable.

decisions.selected: Twenty-four hours after run creation, with cutoff capped at maturity.
decisions.rationale: The intended comment is immediate, while a fixed one-day window allows delayed delivery and produces stable post-maturity observations.

decisions.selected: Binary direct attainment: matching link comment is 1, otherwise 0; unavailable evidence is null.
decisions.rationale: A posted link is the exact intended repository outcome and supports one authoritative value in [0,1].
The workflow's first commit has no parent and no pre-adoption workflow or accepted outcome evidence is available in the repository.

decisions.selected: Expose only missing-reason and run identity diagnostics; never combine them with value.
decisions.rationale: Diagnostics support data-quality review without treating execution activity as operational attainment.

uncertainties.description: Historical runs without archived case and event can have multiple qualifying /ace comments near run creation.
uncertainties.mitigation: Use the latest qualifying comment before creation and retain bounded-ambiguity classification.

uncertainties.description: GitHub comment history may be unavailable to the evaluator or truncated by API access.
No comparable pre-adoption evidence exists because the adoption commit is the repository root.
